propositions: A Jira issue's KEY changes when moved between projects while its numeric id is immutable, and third-party moves can fail to update the moved_issue_key table so the old key stops resolving.
Because rebar bindings are keyed pervasively on the jira_key, a moved issue can silently detach and be retired by the absence probe even though the issue still exists.

The fix additively records the numeric jira_id on each binding and, on a key-lookup miss, resolves by id and re-keys the binding to the current key while updating the reverse index in the same operation.

The change is additive rather than re-keying the cloud-shared store, so existing jira_key-taking methods keep their signatures and legacy bindings without a recorded id work unchanged with no migration.
The id fallback must not fire when the key still resolves, and genuine deletions (failing by both key and id) must still retire so recovery does not mask a real absence.

What GET /rest/api/2/issue/{oldKey} returns for a moved issue on DC 8.17.1 stays unsettled because a project move is not performable through the authoritative client, so the fix was designed correct under all three readings.
